author: Ashley Belanger
summary_long: In a bankruptcy proceeding that kicked off yesterday, Disney has offered to buy some of the technology that powers the controversy-plagued chatbot Character.AI. title: Topgolf saved over $11.3 million after leaving VMware
author: Scharon Harding
summary_long: Topgolf’s VMware costs were going to increase by 400 percent under Broadcom. To avoid that cost, the sports entertainment company moved 12,000 virtual machines (VMs) to VergeIO’s VergeOS and has saved over $11 million so far. Before migrating, Topgolf’s VMware connection “ran very deep,” Scott Forehand, Topgolf’s global infrastructure manager, told Ars Technica. Topgolf has over 100 locations worldwide featuring interactive golf games with real-time shot tracking and digital analytics. Source: arstechnica.com. Date: 2026-10-13. id: bigtech:martin shkreli livestreamed himself violating lifetime pharm:2026-10-13T22:48:12.000Z
title: Martin Shkreli livestreamed himself violating lifetime pharma ban, FTC says
author: Beth Mole
summary_long: Martin Shkreli—the ex-pharmaceutical executive infamous for illegally hiking the price of a lifesaving anti-parasitic drug by more than 4,000 percent and getting a seven-year prison sentence for the fraudulent scheme he used to do it—has been under a lifetime ban from the pharmaceutical industry since 2022. However, according to the Federal Trade Commission and the attorneys general of seven states, Shkreli has "flagrantly and repeatedly" violated that ban nearly the entire time—allegedly by trading stock in dozens of drug companies and discussing the industry during livestreams on social media. On Tuesday, the FTC and the seven states asked a federal judge to hold Shkreli in contempt for the alleged violations. The states include New York, California, Illinois, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Virginia—the same states that joined the FTC in suing Shkreli in 2020 over the "elaborate anticompetitive scheme" involving the anti-parasitic drug, Daraprim. Source: arstechnica.com. Date: 2026-10-13. Why it matters: outline likely impact on technology, business, or society.

id: ai_data:tev scaling longhorizon agentic environments with dense prog:2026-10-13T17:59:51.000Z
title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
author: Wenbo Hu
summary_long: Long-horizon agents have drawn growing attention for their ability to work autonomously -- from hours to days -- on economically valuable tasks, a capability essential to automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet open-source models still struggle on long-horizon tasks, largely for lack of both training data and a working recipe, and scaling both is hard: long, complex tasks are difficult to curate and verify, and their rewards are sparse. We address both. First, we introduce Tev-Gym, the first long-horizon agent training dataset with verifiable, dense, progressive rewards -- 1,170 verified task environments across 7 domains. id: ai_data:doubtless trainingfree contrastive decoding for efficient re:2026-10-13T17:59:32.000Z
title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning
author: Minghao Luo
summary_long: Reasoning models achieve strong performance through long chains of thought (CoT), but often spend more tokens than needed to solve a problem. Existing ways to shorten the CoT require additional training for each model, add a fixed steering vector to the model's hidden states, or use decoding heuristics such as stopping early or banning words like "wait", which can reduce accuracy. We propose DoubtLess, a training-free decoding method in which a much smaller reasoning model steers the large one towards brevity. The small model reads the large model's CoT so far twice, once prompted to be brief (the brief thinker) and once prompted to be verbose (the verbose thinker), and the difference between its two logit vectors, scaled by a strength, is added to the large model's logits at every step of the CoT. Source: arxiv.org. Date: 2026-10-13. Why it matters: outline likely impact on technology, business, or society. What’s next: note near-term developments or signals to watch.

id: space:spacex launches nasa science and cargo to the international :2026-10-13T14:07:50.000Z
title: SpaceX launches NASA science and cargo to the International Space Station
author: Will Robinson-Smith
summary_long: Under the soft glow of sunrise Tuesday morning, SpaceX’s Falcon 9 rocket roared away from pad 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station at 6:33 a.m. EDT (1033 UTC) to begin a cargo run to the International Space Station. The 35th Commercial Resupply Services (CRS-35) is carrying more than 6,300 pounds of science and supplies to the orbiting outpost when it docks to the space-facing port of the Harmony module on Thursday morning. Fewer than 7.5 minutes after leaving the launch pad, the first stage booster, tail number B1096, wrapped up its eighth trip to space and back with a landing at Landing Zone 40 adjacent to the pad.
